# Desktop session

The GNU root runs a Weston kiosk session as `desktop`, uid 1001, with seatd, Debian's udev daemon and PulseAudio. `init-metal` supervises `rach2-desktop`, which starts the device services at boot and the user session only on SIGHUP, so that a boot leaves the screen and the keyboard to the console's login. Its output goes to `/var/log/services`.

## Use

The account has a locked password and belongs to `seat`, `video`, `render`, `kvm`, `input` and `audio`. Root can enter it with `su -s /bin/bash desktop`. Its private runtime directory is `/run/user/1001`, created at boot with mode 0700. `kill -HUP $(cat /run/rach2-desktop.pid)` starts the session and `kill -USR2 $(cat /run/rach2-desktop.pid)` ends it; the supervisor logs `rach2-desktop: services: up; SIGHUP starts the session` once the device services run, and `rach2-desktop: session: stopped; SIGHUP starts it again` after SIGUSR2. A test that starts the session ends it the same way, so that it leaves the console as it found it. Set `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1001`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0` and `PULSE_SERVER=unix:/run/user/1001/pulse/native` when starting a program there from another session.

`/etc/xdg/weston/weston.ini` selects kiosk-shell, Xwayland and no idle blanking. The session chooses headless with Pixman when no DRM connector is connected. A connected display uses DRM with Pixman, or GL when its card has a render node; of several cards with a connected connector, the first by number with a render node, then the first of the others, which Weston opens alone with `--drm-device`. Weston's log in `/var/log/services` names the renderer and each output's modes, the current one marked. To set an output's resolution, add `[output]` with `name=Virtual-1` and `mode=1024x768` to `weston.ini` and restart the session with SIGHUP to the supervisor. When Weston ends, by a signal or by quitting, the session ends and the console takes the screen and keyboard back; SIGHUP to the supervisor starts it again. When the session's card goes away, as when the test bed's VM that drew it dies or Rach2's driver gives the GPU to a VM, the supervisor starts the session again on the displays left, headless with GL on llvmpipe when none is, and then on the next card with a connected connector that appears, which brings it back to the GPU once Rach2's driver has it again. Stop the supervisor to restart the device services as well; init starts it again. Each supervisor ends and reaps its children on exit. [desktop(7)](../../../man/man7/desktop.7) gives the display's details.

## Design

`rach2-desktop` makes `/tmp/.X11-unix` and `/tmp/.ICE-unix`, mode 1777, as Debian's `tmpfiles.d/x11.conf` does at boot, since Weston's Xwayland module binds its listening socket there and Weston 14.0.2 exits with a segmentation fault when that bind fails. It starts systemd-udevd outside systemd, waits for its control socket to answer, triggers existing devices and settles their events. It starts seatd with `SEATD_VTBOUND=0` because Rach2 has no VT interface. The seat socket belongs to the `seat` group. The session starts, on SIGHUP, only after that socket exists, under the desktop account's supplementary groups and a private D-Bus session bus. The image's udmabuf rule gives `/dev/udmabuf` mode 0660 and group `kvm`, which the desktop account belongs to ([udmabuf](../../../rach2/sys/dmabuf/Readme.md)). udevd runs with `--resolve-names=early`, so that Debian's rules give the DRM nodes the groups `video` and `render` and the event devices `input`; with `never` it would leave every node root's group. The supervisor writes its pid to `/run/rach2-desktop.pid` and runs the session as a process group of its own; SIGHUP ends that group with TERM and CONT, waits until none of it is left without blocking on any one process, since Weston holds its socket's lock until it exits, kills what is left after 10 seconds, and starts a new session; SIGUSR2 ends the session the same way and starts none; a session that ends is not started again until SIGHUP, so that a killed Weston leaves the console its screen. The supervisor chooses the display, `BACKEND CARD RENDERER`, and gives it to `rach2-session` as its arguments; it keeps the card's device in `/sys`, so that a card of the same name made later for another device counts as the old one gone. A child runs `udevadm monitor` on the `drm` subsystem and sends the supervisor SIGUSR1 for each card added or removed, and names each removed card first in `/run/rach2-desktop.removed`, which it only appends to and the supervisor reads past the lines it has read, so that no removal is lost between them, and so that a card that goes away and comes back under the same name and device before the supervisor looks still counts as gone: when the session's card is gone, or Weston ended and its card with it, the session starts again, and while it has lost its card, a card that appears starts it again there. A start on a card ends that wait, whether it came by a card appearing, by SIGHUP or at once after the loss, when the card came back before the old session had gone. Headless after such a loss is GL, so that the session's compositing goes on in software on llvmpipe; headless otherwise stays Pixman. The supervisor checks its signal flags and children once a second. It checks for card loss before applying SIGHUP and again after stopping the old session, so a restart during removal keeps the wait for a replacement card. A device service that ends makes the supervisor exit, so that init restarts the whole.

`rach2-session` runs PulseAudio and Weston in the foreground. PulseAudio runs `/etc/pulse/rach2.pa` alone, not Debian's `default.pa`; it loads `module-oss` over `/dev/dsp` without mmap, as the sink `oss_output` and the source `oss_input`, whose names differ since PulseAudio keeps one namespace for both, and exposes the user's native PulseAudio socket. It opens the device at 48 kHz, the rate the kernel mixes at, so that PulseAudio converts each client's rate in user space, as a sound server on Linux does, and the kernel's audio thread copies the frames through instead of resampling each with its windowed-sinc filter. It also loads `module-suspend-on-idle`, as PulseAudio's default configuration does: after five seconds without a client that needs a sink or source, that endpoint suspends. Once both suspend, the OSS module closes `/dev/dsp`, stopping the device's streams when no other open uses them; the next client resumes its endpoint. Without the idle module, OSS keeps writing silence and reading capture while idle. A machine without sound can still start the session. `/etc/asound.conf` gives ALSA clients a `plug` conversion over the OSS plugin. Both routes use the kernel's mixer; the ALSA default opens OSS directly. Programs that use PulseAudio find its socket through `PULSE_SERVER`.

## Building

`install_root.sh` installs the scripts and configuration after the Debian packages and locks the account the manifest supplies. The root image depends on every file here. `make ARCH=x86_64 os-real-gnu-ext2` rebuilds the image after an edit.

## Tests

The `desktop` family boots the GNU root with `rach2.audio.loopback`. Each case starts the session by SIGHUP. Its headless case reads the compositor's uid, the seat socket, the input properties and the browser and ALSA tones recorded through OSS. It leaves the normal browser sandbox enabled. Its display cases boot the `std-vga` and `virtio-vga` profiles and run [`tests/graphics/desktop_display.py`](../../../tests/graphics/desktop_display.py): first [`tests/graphics/bootscreen.sh`](../../../tests/graphics/bootscreen.sh) on the fresh boot, which finds no Weston and the console holding its card with the keyboard, then Weston's DRM output and renderer, the nodes' groups, both browsers taking keys and a click through QMP, `weston-simple-egl`, two modes through `weston.ini`, and the console's scanout and keyboard after Weston's SIGKILL; on i686, evdev, an llvmpipe render and modetest.
